name: Special Region of Yogyakarta
summary_text: Yogyakarta is among the eight provinces whose regional regulations OutRight's Creeping Criminalisation study examined as discriminatory, and is one of the eight (with North Sumatra) for which no specific enforcement incident, police action, or enacted anti-LGBT bylaw targeting transgender people was documented in the dossier. The signal is legal divergence without operational evidence. Despite its special administrative status and cultural prominence, no trans-specific incident was found; the OutRight finding confirms a regulatory layer but does not demonstrate enforcement against visitors. Deviation from the national score (0.15) is −0.02, the minimum reporting threshold; Yogyakarta shares this minimal-divergence tier with North Sumatra. It sits above the operational-enforcement provinces (Aceh 0.03, West Java 0.08, West Sumatra 0.11) where raids, corporal punishment or enacted bylaws exist, below the capital territory (0.16) - also an OutRight focus province - and below Bali (0.22), which has no documented regulatory signal and benefits from tourism-economy tolerance.

sources.claim_summary: OutRight Action International, 'Creeping Criminalisation: Mapping of Indonesia's National Laws and Regional Regulations That Violate Human Rights of Women and LGBTIQ People' (Katjasungkana & Wieringa; 2022 file copy): maps national laws and discriminatory regional regulations, examining regional regulations in eight focus provinces - Aceh, DKI Jakarta, East Kalimantan, Lampung, North Sumatra, South Sulawesi, South Sumatra and Yogyakarta - finding much overlap but significant regional variation (dress codes, curfews, restrictions on where transgender people may appear), and states that its findings are valid for regions beyond the focus set.
